scenes.text: In part one, we learned attention, how words look at each other. [1] But how does a transformer go from your prompt to a full answer? [2] In part two, let's follow a sentence through the machine.

Here's the journey, for the prompt, the capital of India is. [1] First, the text is split into tokens. [2] Each token becomes an embedding, plus a signal for its position in the sentence. [3] The tokens pass through many transformer layers, each with attention, and a small thinking step. [4] At the end, the model scores every possible next token, [5] picks one, New, and repeats, to get Delhi.

Each transformer layer does two jobs. [1] Think of it as a team meeting, followed by some private thinking. [2] In the attention step, every token gathers information from the others. [3] In the feed forward step, each token thinks about what it learned, on its own. [4] Stack dozens of these layers, and the understanding gets deeper and deeper.

data.definition: One round of attention (tokens share information) plus a feed-forward step (each token thinks alone).

scenes.text: Now, one sneaky problem. Attention looks at all the words at once, so how does it know word order? [1] Dog bites man, and man bites dog, use exactly the same words. [2] So each token gets a position signal added to it, first, second, third. [3] And now the model knows who bit whom.

data.heading: Word order matters
steps: Now it knows who bit whom

scenes.text: And at the very end, it's next token prediction, from episode two. [1] The model scores every possible next token. New is the most likely, and Mumbai is much less likely. [2] It picks New, [3] then runs again, and adds Delhi.

Here are four words to know. [1] Parameters, the numbers inside all these layers, often billions of them. [2] Layers, how many rounds of attention and thinking there are. [3] Context length, how many tokens it can look at, at once. [4] And decoder, the type of transformer chatbots use, which writes one token at a time.

data.heading: Transformer words
terms: Tokens it can see at once
Writes one token at a time

scenes.text: Here's a common myth. [1] People think a transformer looks up answers in a stored database of facts. [2] It doesn't. Its knowledge is spread across billions of parameters, as patterns. That's why it can be brilliant, and also why it can confidently get facts wrong.

data.myth: A transformer looks up answers in a database of facts.
data.fact: Knowledge is spread across billions of parameters as patterns, which is why it can also be wrong.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! How does a transformer know that, dog bites man, is different from, man bites dog? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] Position signals! Each token knows where it sits in the sentence.

Let's recap. [1] Text is split into tokens, and turned into embeddings. [2] Position signals keep track of word order. [3] Stacked layers of attention and thinking build understanding. [4] And at the end, it predicts the next token. [5] Next, we'll learn how AI sees images, with computer vision. Follow AI Maastaaru!
